correctness.rationale: For A=xH+yC with Picard intersection matrix [[4,5],[5,2]], positivity against both effective (−2) curves D=2H−C, D′=−2H+9C yields p=3x+8y>0, q=37x+8y>0. Since a third irreducible (−2) class would intersect both nonnegatively, the quadratic identity (p²+66pq+q²)/2176=−2 forbids it. The chamber thus gives ampleness. A²≤16 implies pq≤527; exact divisibility x=(q−p)/34, y=(37p−3q)/272 and primitivity give squares/classes {2:C;4:H,−H+5C;8:3H−C,−3H+14C;16:H+C,−H+6C}; excludes 6,10,12,14. Independent integer (p,q) enumeration exhausts the bounded domain and involution x→−x,y→5x+y pairs. This is finite proof for a finite low-degree window, not the entire spectrum.
